blocks.text: 1. Max Pooling

blocks.alt: A window has its maximum value taken, forming max pooling

blocks.text: Pooling, the previous topic, introduced summarizing a small region into a single output value. Max Pooling is a complete, dedicated look at Pooling's most common variant, explored in full depth throughout this topic.
It works by keeping only the genuinely largest value within each small window, a genuinely simple, direct summarization rule covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. The Rule

blocks.alt: Each window keeps only the largest value

blocks.text: This connects back to the pooling window, already covered in Pooling. At each position, examine every value inside that small window, following the same sliding pattern already covered there.
Keep only the genuinely single largest one, discarding every other value in that region, a genuinely direct, simple rule that gives Max Pooling its own distinctive name.

blocks.text: 3. Why Max Specifically

blocks.alt: The strongest activation is the most important signal

blocks.text: A genuinely intuitive justification connects back to feature maps, already covered in the Convolution Operation. A genuinely large activation value signals that a filter's pattern was genuinely strongly detected there.
This makes the maximum value within a region a genuinely meaningful summary, directly representing the strongest evidence of that filter's pattern being present anywhere within that small window.
4. Keeping The Strongest Signal

blocks.alt: Max pooling preserves the strongest features

blocks.text: This connects back to why max specifically, already covered in this topic. Keeping the maximum genuinely preserves the strongest evidence that a pattern was present, rather than diluting it with weaker, surrounding values.

This holds even if its genuinely exact position within the small window shifts slightly, since the maximum value itself, already covered, gets preserved regardless of exactly where within the window it happened to occur.
5. Recapping Translation Invariance

This connects back to strengthening translation invariance, already covered in Pooling. Max Pooling genuinely delivers this benefit especially strongly, more so than a generic pooling operation might.

This happens since a small shift in exactly where a pattern appears often still yields the exact same maximum value, exactly the property already covered as keeping the strongest signal in the previous section.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This especially strong translation invariance, already covered in this topic, is one of the main reasons Max Pooling became the genuinely dominant pooling choice across most practical Convolutional Neural Network architectures.

blocks.text: 6. A Genuinely Useful Sparsity Effect

blocks.alt: Max pooling gives a sparser representation

blocks.text: A genuinely useful side effect connects back to feature maps often containing many genuinely low or zero values, already covered implicitly with ReLU in the Activation Functions module.

Max Pooling naturally emphasizes the genuinely few, strongest activations in each region, effectively filtering out the many weaker, less meaningful values that ReLU, already covered, often leaves behind.
7. Common Window Sizes In Practice

blocks.alt: A common window size is 2 by 2

blocks.text: A genuinely common, real practical convention applies here. A 2x2 window with stride 2, already covered in the previous topic, is the genuinely most common configuration for Max Pooling.

This reduces both height and width by genuinely half at each pooling layer, a genuinely predictable, standard reduction pattern used throughout many established Convolutional Neural Network architectures.
8. Max Pooling Versus A Preview Of Average Pooling
This connects back to Average Pooling, covered in the very next topic of this module. Max Pooling keeps only the genuinely strongest signal; Average Pooling instead smooths across the entire region.
These are two genuinely different summarization philosophies, both already introduced in Pooling, with the very next topic exploring the Average Pooling side of this contrast in complete depth.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Max Pooling Is Genuinely The Right Choice

blocks.alt: Detecting the presence of a feature points toward using max pooling

blocks.text: This connects back to detecting whether a specific pattern is genuinely present anywhere in a region. Max Pooling, already covered in this topic, directly answers exactly that question through its own maximum-value rule.

This is also the genuinely most common, standard default choice throughout most Convolutional Neural Network architectures, where Max Pooling remains genuinely the most widely used pooling variant in practice.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates Max Pooling's core computation, applying a 2x2 window with stride 2 to a small feature map, illustrating the rule already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

feature_map = np.array([
    [1, 3, 2, 4],
    [5, 6, 1, 2],
    [7, 2, 9, 4],
    [3, 1, 0, 8],
])

pool_size = 2
stride = 2  # already covered as the common window size configuration in this topic

output_size = (feature_map.shape[0] - pool_size) // stride + 1
max_pooled = np.zeros((output_size, output_size))

for i in range(output_size):
    for j in range(output_size):
        row, col = i * stride, j * stride
        region = feature_map[row:row + pool_size, col:col + pool_size]
        max_pooled[i, j] = region.max()  # already covered as the rule in this topic

print("Original feature map:\n", feature_map)
print("\nMax pooled output:\n", max_pooled)
print("\nEach output value is the genuinely single largest value from its corresponding 2x2 region, already covered as the rule in this topic")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows each output value matching the genuinely largest value from its corresponding region, exactly the simple, direct rule already covered as this topic's own core mechanism.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Max Pooling keeps only the largest value within each small pooling window.
A large activation value signals that a filter's pattern was strongly detected in that region.
This preserves the strongest evidence of a pattern's presence, regardless of its exact position within the window.
Max Pooling especially strengthens translation invariance, since small shifts often still yield the same maximum.
It naturally emphasizes the few strongest activations, filtering out weaker values.
A 2x2 window with stride 2 is the most common configuration, halving height and width.
It contrasts with Average Pooling, which smooths across the entire region instead.
It remains the most widely used pooling variant across most practical architectures.
